font.reason: Weight 900 gives uniform heavy monoline strokes that read as the thick disjoint stroke segments of the original; Lalezar was too blobby once cut, Reem Kufi's final ه became illegible when fragmented. Caption uses Vazirmatn 800 (variable, real bold). Loaded via FaRoot.

comps.translatedSummary: Title 'SHIP' becomes the Persian word «عرضه»; caption becomes «ساخت واژه از پاره‌خط‌ها». 16 disjoint fragments of the real typeset word light in scrambled order, last 3 are the key fragments, final scale pulse 1→1.06→1.

rtlDecisions.why: Persian letters connect and are curved, so the hand-drawn straight butt-cap line segments cannot be reused. The word is typeset once and 16 rectangular slices (clip-path inset, 10px gaps) are revealed; never split into code points, so shaping stays correct.
Horizontal fragments travel right->left (the original left->right was reading direction); vertical fragments keep top->bottom (physical).
New 16-entry order spread across letters; last 3 (ع bowl, ر tail, ض dot) are the recognition keys, preserving the 'unreadable first 70%' design.
Motion beats unchanged; 16 fragments retained so beats are identical; composition is symmetric.
Tracking breaks Persian joining; replaced by Vazirmatn 800 at fs(44), centered like the original.
Symmetric about the vertical axis; flex-centered so direction:rtl does not shift it.

rasterTextHandling: No raster assets in this card.
concerns: At f95 (13 of 16 fragments lit) the right part ه/ض/ر is partly guessable by a Persian reader; an alternative ORDER could hide one more body fragment of ه if a stronger mystery is wanted.
Seams (10px gaps) remain visible in the final held word, as the original's segments were also disjoint.
lessons: Stroke-built / line-segment title effects cannot be redrawn as straight segments for Persian: typeset the real word and reveal disjoint clip-path rectangles of it (translate each fragment with its own clip applied before transform).
Pick the fragmenting font by cutting it: Reem Kufi and Lalezar looked fine whole but fragmented badly; Vazirmatn 900 stayed legible.
